nodes.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.
nodes.label: 1.G.A.1

nodes.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.
nodes.label: 4.G.A.2

nodes.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.
nodes.label: 3.G.A.1

nodes.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/“corners”) and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).
nodes.label: K.G.B.4

nodes.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.
nodes.label: K.G.A.2

nodes.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

nodes.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.
nodes.label: K.G.B.5

nodes.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three- dimensional (“solid”).
